title: Read Aloud
summary: Read a short passage aloud.
instructions: Read the text silently during preparation. After the tone, read it aloud exactly as written.
tips: Notice punctuation and group words into meaningful phrases.
Keep a comfortable pace and make the last word of each phrase clear.
Listen back against the text and mark omissions.
pitfall: Do not restart the whole sentence after a small slip.
scoring: Content, pronunciation and oral fluency. Focus on intelligibility, not imitating an accent.

title: Repeat Sentence
summary: Listen once, then repeat the sentence.
instructions: Listen without writing a full transcript. When recording begins, repeat the sentence in the same order.
tips: Hold the meaning in short chunks.
Follow the stress of the original sentence.
Say the words you remember in sequence.
pitfall: Adding your own ending changes the content.
scoring: Correct word sequences, pronunciation and oral fluency.

title: Describe Image
summary: Turn a visual into a clear spoken description.
instructions: Study the image for 25 seconds. After the tone, describe its main features and relationships.
tips: Identify the topic and units first.
Select two important comparisons or changes.
End with an observation supported by the image.
pitfall: Do not invent causes that the visual does not show.
scoring: Relevant, specific content, pronunciation and oral fluency.

title: Retell Lecture
summary: Explain a short lecture in your own words.
instructions: Listen once and take brief notes. After 10 seconds of preparation, retell the main ideas.
tips: Write a topic, two supporting points and a conclusion.
Use links such as because and however to preserve relationships.
Practise turning notes into complete spoken sentences.
pitfall: A list of isolated keywords is difficult to follow.
scoring: Accuracy and coverage of ideas, pronunciation and oral fluency.

title: Answer Short Question
summary: Give a short factual answer to an audio question.
instructions: Listen to the question. As soon as recording opens, answer with one word or a short phrase.
tips: Identify the category being asked for.
Use the simplest accurate term.
Speak promptly and clearly.
pitfall: A longer explanation does not earn extra credit.
scoring: Whether your answer correctly addresses the question; this task contributes to Listening.

title: Summarize Group Discussion
summary: Connect the views of three speakers.
instructions: Listen to the three-person discussion. Prepare for 10 seconds, then summarize it in your own words in up to two minutes.
tips: Make three columns for speaker notes.
Capture agreement, disagreement and the final direction.
Introduce the topic, connect the views, and finish with the outcome.
pitfall: Do not attribute one speaker’s opinion to someone else.
scoring: Coverage, accurate relationships between ideas, pronunciation and oral fluency.

title: Respond to a Situation
summary: Say what you would actually say in a situation.
instructions: Read and listen to the situation. After 10 seconds, speak directly to the person described.
tips: Identify who you are speaking to and what you need.
Use a suitable level of politeness.
Include the important practical details and a clear request.
pitfall: Do not narrate what you would do instead of speaking to the person.
scoring: Relevance, effective communication, pronunciation and oral fluency.

title: Summarize Written Text
summary: Summarize a passage in one sentence.
instructions: Read the passage and write one complete sentence of 5–75 words. You have 10 minutes.
tips: Find the main claim and its essential support.
Join related ideas with an appropriate conjunction.
Check that the result is one grammatical sentence.
pitfall: Multiple sentences or a list do not meet the required form.
scoring: Content, form, grammar and vocabulary. This app provides a model, not an official score.

title: Write Essay
summary: Develop an argument in 200–300 words.
instructions: Write an essay of 200–300 words responding to the prompt. You have 20 minutes, including planning and checking.
tips: Take a position that answers the exact question.
Develop each main point with a reason and an example.
Reserve time to check grammar and word count.
pitfall: Memorized generic paragraphs may fail to address the prompt.
scoring: Content, form, organization, language range, grammar, vocabulary and spelling.

title: Fill in the Blanks (Dropdown)
summary: Choose a word for each gap in a passage.
instructions: Select the option that fits each blank. Use grammar and the meaning of the whole passage.
tips: Predict the part of speech before opening the options.
Check common word partnerships.
Reread the completed sentence.
pitfall: A word can be grammatically possible but wrong in context.
scoring: Each correct blank earns credit. This task focuses on reading comprehension and vocabulary in context.

title: Multiple Choice, Multiple Answers
summary: Select every answer supported by a passage.
instructions: Read the passage and select more than one correct option.
tips: Read the question before looking for evidence.
Evaluate each option separately.
Select only claims supported by the text.
pitfall: Incorrect selections deduct points within this item, with a minimum of zero.
scoring: Correct choices minus incorrect choices, floored at zero.

title: Reorder Paragraphs
summary: Put a scrambled passage back in order.
instructions: Select a Source paragraph, then use the arrow to place it in order in Target.
tips: Find an opening that does not depend on earlier information.
Track pronouns and repeated nouns.
Check time, cause and contrast between adjacent sentences.
pitfall: A sentence starting with this result usually needs a preceding cause.
scoring: Credit for correct adjacent pairs, not just a correct opening.

title: Fill in the Blanks (Drag and Drop)
summary: Complete a passage from a shared word bank.
instructions: Drag words into the gaps. You can also select a word and then a gap using the keyboard.
tips: Read the whole passage first.
Use grammar to narrow the word bank.
Check meaning after every placement.
pitfall: There are extra words; you do not need to use all of them.
scoring: Each correctly completed gap earns credit.

title: Multiple Choice, Single Answer
summary: Find the one best answer to a reading question.
instructions: Read the text and choose one answer.
tips: Identify whether the question asks for a main idea or a detail.
Eliminate answers contradicted by the text.
Choose the option that answers the whole question.
pitfall: A true detail may still fail to answer the question asked.
scoring: One correct answer; no partial credit.

title: Summarize Spoken Text
summary: Write a concise summary of a recording.
instructions: Listen once and write a 50–70 word summary. The 10 minutes include listening and writing.
tips: Note the central claim and essential support.
Use your own connected sentences.
Leave time to check spelling and the 50–70 word target.
pitfall: Do not spend all your time transcribing examples and miss the conclusion.
scoring: Content, form, grammar, vocabulary and spelling; model-based self-review here.

title: Multiple Choice, Multiple Answers
summary: Select all the claims supported by audio.
instructions: Listen once, then choose every correct answer.
tips: Preview the question during the countdown.
Listen for changes of opinion and qualifications.
Evaluate the meaning of each option.
pitfall: Incorrect choices subtract credit, so avoid selecting everything.
scoring: Correct selections minus incorrect selections, with a zero minimum.

title: Fill in the Blanks (Type In)
summary: Type the missing words in a transcript.
instructions: Listen to the recording and type the exact missing word into each gap.
tips: Follow the transcript while listening.
Move through gaps with Tab.
Check plurals and spelling before moving on.
pitfall: A correct-sounding word with the wrong spelling loses credit.
scoring: Each correctly spelled missing word earns credit.

title: Highlight Correct Summary
summary: Choose the summary that captures the recording.
instructions: Listen once and select the paragraph that best summarizes the main ideas.
tips: Note the topic and the speaker’s conclusion.
Check that the summary preserves cause and contrast.
Reject options that add unsupported conclusions.
pitfall: An option repeating several words can still reverse the meaning.
scoring: One correct summary; no partial credit.

title: Multiple Choice, Single Answer
summary: Choose one answer after listening.
instructions: Listen once and select the best answer to the question.
tips: Preview the question during the countdown.
Listen for the requested detail or purpose.
Wait for the full recording before settling on an option.
pitfall: The speaker may mention an option only to reject it.
scoring: One correct choice; no partial credit.

title: Select Missing Word
summary: Predict the end of an audio passage.
instructions: Listen to the recording, which ends before the final word or phrase. Select the missing ending.
tips: Follow the topic and direction of the argument.
Use meaning as well as grammar.
Choose the ending that completes the speaker’s thought.
pitfall: Picking an option just because it was mentioned earlier can mislead you.
scoring: One correct ending; no partial credit.

title: Highlight Incorrect Words
summary: Find differences between speech and a transcript.
instructions: Listen once while reading. Select words in the text that differ from the audio.
tips: Follow the text at the speaker’s pace.
Click only when you hear a mismatch.
Use surrounding words to keep your place.
pitfall: Extra selections lose credit; do not highlight unfamiliar words at random.
scoring: Correctly identified differences minus incorrect selections, floored at zero.

title: Write from Dictation
summary: Type a sentence exactly as you hear it.
instructions: Listen once and type the sentence. Check your spelling before moving on.
tips: Remember short meaningful phrases.
Reconstruct the sentence in the correct order.
Check articles, endings and plural nouns.
pitfall: Do not omit small grammatical words such as the or a.
scoring: Correctly spelled words receive credit. Local feedback checks the full sentence; it is not an official scoring engine.
